symbols.name: R
symbols.def: \(R(Z)\) is the explicitly indexed finite domain of \(Z\).

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: The supplied full causal graph, with every vertex in \(U\) a root.

symbols.name: F
symbols.type: family of total set-valued local tables

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: \(a\) is a supplied solution of \(M\).

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: \(L\) is the number of indexed domain entries, vertices, edges, table rows, parent-coordinate incidences, output incidences, actual-value records, and cost records in the explicit input.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: \(B\) is the total binary length of all numerators and denominators in \(c\), together with the budget when one is supplied.

symbols.name: AZ
symbols.def: \(A_Z(r)=\{a_Z\}\) at the actual parent row and \(A_Z(r)=F_Z(r)\) otherwise.

symbols.name: SZ
symbols.def: \(S_Z=\operatorname{Pa}_H(Z)\).

symbols.name: QZ
symbols.def: \(Q_Z^{S_Z}(b)=\bigcup_{r:r|_{S_Z}=b}A_Z(r)\).

symbols.name: DeltaZ
symbols.def: For \(t\in A_Z(r)\setminus\{a_Z\}\), \(\Delta_Z(r)=\{p\in\operatorname{Pa}_G(Z):r_p\ne a_p\}\).

symbols.name: Mexp
symbols.def: The class defined by \(\mathrm{def:explicit-class}\).

symbols.name: Mforest
symbols.def: The class defined by \(\mathrm{def:forest-class}\).

symbols.name: Ppath
symbols.def: When \(X\) reaches \(Y\), \(P_0=X\to P_1\to\cdots\to P_m=Y\) is their unique directed path in a full causal polyforest.

symbols.name: Wi
symbols.def: \(W_i=\operatorname{Pa}_G(P_i)\setminus\{P_{i-1}\}\).

symbols.name: Safei
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Safe}_i(D)\) holds iff \(\bigcup_{b:b_q=a_q\ \forall q\in W_i\setminus D}A_{P_i}(a_{P_{i-1}},b)=\{a_{P_i}\}\).

symbols.name: Ci
symbols.def: For nonactual \(s\in R(P_{i-1})\) and \(t\in R(P_i)\), \(C_i(s,t)\) is the minimum of \(\sum_{q\in D_i(b)}c(q\to P_i)\) over rows \((s,b)\) with \(t\in A_{P_i}(s,b)\) and \(\operatorname{Safe}_i(D_i(b))\), where \(D_i(b)=\{q\in W_i:b_q\ne a_q\}\); the empty minimum is \(+\infty\).

symbols.name: di
symbols.def: \(d_0(s)=0\) for nonactual \(s\in R(X)\), and \(d_i(t)=\min_s\{d_{i-1}(s)+C_i(s,t)\}\).

symbols.name: OPT
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{OPT}=\min_{t\ne a_Y}d_m(t)\).

symbols.name: Cplus
symbols.def: A retained graph, alternate value of \(X\), alternate full state, and one supporting original-table row for every projected membership claim.

symbols.name: Copt
symbols.def: A positive certificate together with all finite \(d_i\) labels, predecessor choices, and local supporting rows attaining \(\operatorname{OPT}\).

symbols.name: Cminus
symbols.def: Either a full-graph reachability cut separating \(X\) from \(Y\), or the layerwise reachable sets of nonactual values ending in the empty set.

symbols.name: Compiler
symbols.def: The explicit-table subset-transform and min-plus construction in \(\mathrm{def:compiler-handle}\).

symbols.name: Verifier
symbols.def: The replay verifier in \(\mathrm{def:verifier-handle}\).

symbols.name: Mchain
symbols.def: The class defined by \(\mathrm{def:chain-class}\).

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.role: Length parameter for the shared-exogenous-selector obstruction family.

symbols.name: Oselector
symbols.type: family of deterministic binary SCM instances
symbols.def: \(\mathcal O_{\kappa}\) is the shared-exogenous-selector family defined by \(\mathrm{def:selector\mbox{-}obstruction\mbox{-}family}\).

symbols.name: UnicycleHandle
symbols.def: Cut the unique undirected full-graph cycle at each boundary edge and augment value-path states by the two-arc reachability signature needed to audit deleted-edge legality; determine whether the resulting finite-state composition is complete or yields a hardness obstruction.

assumptions.condition: \(U\cap V=\varnothing\), both sets are finite, and every \(R(Z)\) is finite and nonempty.

novel.justification: Finite explicitly enumerable signatures are a computational-scope restriction chosen for an auditable backend over categorical systems, finite-state controllers, and tabular causal simulators; this restriction is not attributed as a standard assumption of either Beckers or Eiter--Lukasiewicz.

assumptions.condition: Every vertex in \(U\) has indegree zero in \(G\).
\(F_Z(r)\ne\varnothing\) for every \(Z\in V\) and every \(r\in R(\operatorname{Pa}_G(Z))\).
Every value, table row, parent coordinate, allowed output, graph edge, actual value, and rational cost is explicitly indexed and contributes to \(L\) or \(B\).

novel.justification: Complete local support tables are a realistic backend input for finite categorical systems, finite-state controllers, and tabular causal simulators; this novel encoding convention makes every allowed outcome auditable and is not attributed as a standard assumption of either Beckers or Eiter--Lukasiewicz.

assumptions.condition: The undirected graph underlying \(G\) on \(U\cup V\) is a forest.

novel.justification: Requiring the undirected graph on all exogenous and endogenous vertices to be a forest is a backend-motivated restriction that is satisfied by singly connected finite causal networks with unshared exogenous inputs; it is neither a Beckers assumption nor the endogenous causal-tree condition of EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable.

assumptions.condition: \(|F_Z(r)|=1\) for every \(Z\in V\) and every parent row \(r\).
The subgraph of \(G\) induced by \(V\) is one directed chain from \(X\) to \(Y\).

novel.justification: The all-zero convention is satisfied after relabeling the two values of every variable in binary reliability, fault-propagation, and Boolean-controller models; here it strengthens the lower bound rather than supplying algorithmic leverage.

assumptions.condition: Every vertex of \(G\) has total indegree at most four.

definitions.name: Beckers-legal retained graph
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal H(G)=\{H\subseteq G:\forall(p\to Z)\in E(G)\setminus E(H),\ p\not\leadsto_H Z\}\), where \(\leadsto_H\) denotes a nonempty retained directed path.

definitions.name: Minimum-cost value-path certificate
definitions.construction: Choose nonactual values \(s_i\in R(P_i)\setminus\{a_{P_i}\}\) for \(0\le i\le m\); for every \(i\ge1\), choose a row \((s_{i-1},b_i)\) such that \(s_i\in A_{P_i}(s_{i-1},b_i)\) and \(\operatorname{Safe}_i(D_i(b_i))\), and charge exactly \(\sum_i\sum_{q\in D_i(b_i)}c(q\to P_i)\).

definitions.name: Explicit support compiler
definitions.construction: At each path layer, encode off-path difference supports as masks, apply upward Boolean subset propagation to mark every deletion mask containing a bad support, scan nonactual table rows to form the finite transitions \(C_i\), and apply the min-plus recurrence \(d_i(t)=\min_s\{d_{i-1}(s)+C_i(s,t)\}\); retain predecessor rows and reachable-value cuts as certificate data.

definitions.name: Independent replay verifier
definitions.construction: Recompute actualized rows before projection, audit every deleted edge by full-graph reachability, replay each projected-table membership against an original supporting row, complete unassigned variables in topological order, and check either the min-plus inequalities plus an attaining path or the closure of the separating value sets.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal O_{\kappa}\)
definitions.construction: For each \(\kappa\ge2\), take binary exogenous roots \(T_i,F_i\) for \(1\le i\le\kappa\) and the endogenous chain \(X\to S_1\to\cdots\to S_{\kappa}\to C_1\to\cdots\to C_{\kappa}=Y\), all actually zero, with the unintervened table of \(X\) constantly zero. With \(p\) denoting the chain predecessor, for every \(1\le i\le\kappa\) set \(S_i(p,T_i,F_i)=T_i\wedge F_i\) when \(p=0\) and \(S_i(p,T_i,F_i)=T_i\mathbin{\oplus}F_i\) when \(p=1\); add the shared edge \(T_i\to C_i\) and set \(C_i(p,T_i)=p\wedge T_i\). These displayed edges are the full graph, every displayed parent is functionally genuine, and these equations are the total local tables.

definitions.name: Full-unicycle boundary handle
definitions.construction: Use \(\operatorname{UnicycleHandle}\): cut the unique undirected cycle at a boundary edge and carry the two-arc reachability signature jointly with the local nonactual-value state, without positing either a polynomial algorithm or a hardness answer in advance.

statements.statement: For every \(Z\in V\) and \(H\subseteq G\), the actualized projection preserves the actual local row, \(Q_Z^{S_Z}(a_{S_Z})=\{a_Z\}\), if and only if \(S_Z\cap D\ne\varnothing\) for every \(D\in\mathcal B_Z\). This equivalence freezes the original actual row before any deleted coordinate is unioned.
statements.justification: This is the local semantic invariant that turns Beckers legality into an explicit hitting condition without assuming the answer.
statements.gap: Beckers2025Actual defines actualization and generalized parent deletion separately; it does not derive their row-level iff characterization.
statements.consumer: The verifier can reject an invalid simplification by displaying one uncovered bad-row support.

statements.statement: For every instance in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}\) and retained graph \(H\in\mathcal H(G)\), a model is a legal full-setting Beckers structural simplification with retained graph \(H\) if and only if every node satisfies \(Q_Z^{S_Z}(a_{S_Z})=\{a_Z\}\); in that case the canonical pre-actualized projection has actualization exactly \(Q_Z^{S_Z}\), preserves \(H\), and preserves the deletion cost \(\sum_{e\in E(G)\setminus E(H)}c(e)\). Every accepted alternate partial state extends to a complete solution by topological completion.
statements.justification: The lemma closes the main extensional gap between finite compiler records and Beckers's quantified model semantics.
statements.gap: Section 6, Proposition 20 on page 525, with its proof on page 532, of Beckers2025Actual gives existence of a same-signature representative that is also a structural simplification of the original model, but not an explicit arbitrary-domain, cost-preserving replay theorem with certificate completion.
statements.consumer: An implementation can expose a small checkable record rather than asking users to trust an internal search over simplified models.

statements.statement: For every instance in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{forest}}\), \(X=a_X\) is a Beckers actual cause of \(Y=a_Y\) if and only if a value-path certificate exists. Moreover, the minimum deletion cost over all legal witnesses is exactly \(\operatorname{OPT}=\min_{s_i\ne a_{P_i}}\sum_{i=1}^{m}C_i(s_{i-1},s_i)\). If \(X\) does not reach \(Y\), the answer is negative; otherwise the unique full-graph path fixes every off-path retained parent at its actual value and makes the local safe relations complete under composition.
statements.justification: The theorem gives both a semantic characterization and an additive optimum rather than only a decision algorithm.
statements.gap: EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable propagates value sets for Halpern--Pearl causes on an endogenous causal tree; it does not cover actualized deletion relations, full exogenous incidence, arbitrary rational deletion costs, or Beckers counterfactual witnesses.
statements.consumer: The result supplies the exact forest dispatch and minimum-abnormality witness required by an explicit-support backend for the \(\texttt{actualcauses}\) Python package.

statements.statement: There exist total algorithms \(\operatorname{Compiler}\) and \(\operatorname{Verifier}\) such that, for every instance in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{forest}}\), the compiler returns a certificate in \(\mathcal C_{+}\), \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{opt}}\), or \(\mathcal C_{-}\); the verifier accepts exactly the certificates whose decoded claim is true under canonical Beckers causation and deletion cost. A positive or optimality certificate is returned if and only if the cause exists, an optimality certificate reports exactly \(\operatorname{OPT}\), and a separating certificate is returned if and only if no witness exists. Compilation and verification use \(O(L)\) arithmetic and indexed-address operations and polynomial bit time; after common-denominator scaling, every intermediate integer has \(O(B+\log(L+1))\) bits.
statements.justification: This theorem is the unresolved end-to-end obligation: it binds semantics, output records, optimal cost, and the explicit-input resource bound in one contract.
statements.gap: IbrahimRehwaldPretschner2019SAT proves Boolean HP encodings and ReydDiaconescuDessalles2025Search supplies adjustable approximate search; neither proves an exact arbitrary-domain Beckers compiler with independently replayable three-way certificates.
statements.consumer: Package maintainers obtain a reference checker for regression tests and users obtain auditable explanations of positive, optimal, and negative answers.

statements.statement: Deciding whether \(X=0\) is a Beckers actual cause of \(Y=0\) is NP-complete on \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{chain}}\); the budgeted problem remains NP-complete when every edge has cost zero and the budget is zero. NP membership uses the retained graph, alternate full state, and supporting table rows. NP-hardness is by a polynomial reduction from distinct-literal \(3\)-SAT in which shared exogenous selector roots encode one Boolean choice per variable and clause gates lie on the endogenous chain; full-graph reachability legality forces every successful clause input to agree with the selector choice.
statements.justification: The restriction shows that endogenous treewidth and domain size cannot parameterize an exact Beckers backend by themselves.
statements.gap: EiterLukasiewicz2002Complexity and AleksandrowiczEtAl2014 analyze Halpern--Pearl variants; their reductions do not establish hardness for Beckers deletion legality on a deterministic binary endogenous chain of total indegree four.
statements.consumer: The backend can refuse an endogenous-chain fast path when shared exogenous roots create nonforest full incidence.

statements.statement: For every \(\kappa\ge2\), the endogenous graph of \(\mathcal O_{\kappa}\) is one directed causal tree, namely a chain. For each selector \(S_i\), the history deleting \(T_i\to S_i\) and the history deleting \(F_i\to S_i\) both satisfy local actual-row hitting and give the same singleton feasible nonactual endogenous-value set \(\{1\}\). Deleting \(T_i\to C_i\) is also locally safe and admits value \(1\) at the later gate \(C_i\) in both histories. It is nevertheless full-graph legal after deleting \(T_i\to S_i\) and illegal after deleting \(F_i\to S_i\), because the latter history retains the directed path \(T_i\to S_i\to\cdots\to C_i\). Thus a direct transfer that keeps only \(G[V]\) and the unaugmented layer state of families of subsets of the endogenous path-variable domains from the causal-tree recurrence of EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable cannot audit Beckers deletion legality on this parameterized family.
statements.justification: The scalable selector family isolates exactly which full-graph reachability information an endogenous-value state omits.
statements.gap: The earlier UAI version of EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable, Section 4.1 and Theorems 4.2--4.3, proves its Halpern--Pearl causal-tree result by recursively propagating families of subsets of each endogenous path-variable domain. This proposition leaves that theorem untouched and shows only that a direct \(G[V]\)-only transfer of that state type cannot certify Beckers edge-deletion legality.
statements.consumer: A parameterized regression batch over \(\mathcal O_{\kappa}\) detects backends that collapse two selector histories with identical endogenous value states but different full-graph legality.

statements.statement: For explicit finite-domain instances whose undirected full causal graph has exactly one cycle, does the two-arc reachability augmentation specified by \(\operatorname{UnicycleHandle}\) yield a sound-and-complete polynomial-size certificate calculus and polynomial-time decision algorithm, or can the shared-selector hardness mechanism be embedded already in this class? Give either the complete composition theorem or a restriction-preserving hardness reduction.
statements.justification: This is the first structural boundary beyond a full polyforest and exposes the genuinely open content without asserting general treewidth fixed-parameter tractability.
statements.gap: Neither Beckers2025Actual nor the Halpern--Pearl decomposition literature classifies reachability-sensitive deletion semantics on a single full-graph cycle.
statements.consumer: The answer determines the next exact structural dispatch supported by the backend after forests.

sampling_model.design: No statistical sampling; the input is one explicitly encoded finite acyclic NSCM and one designated actual solution.
sampling_model.units: Vertices, domain values, local-table rows, output incidences, graph edges, and rational cost records counted by \(L\).
sampling_model.treatment: The singleton counterfactual intervention changes \(X=a_X\) to some \(X=x'\ne a_X\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; local tables are total and all finite domains are explicitly enumerated.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the local relations are supplied exactly rather than estimated.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 6, Proposition 20 on page 525, proved on page 532, gives a same-signature representative that is both a structural simplification of the original model and a witness to the actual-cause counterfactual dependence.
Acyclic nondeterministic SCMs use set-valued mechanisms and preserve the designated actual solution under counterfactual evaluation.
Bounded-domain, bounded-width causal trees and layered graphs permit polynomial Halpern--Pearl cause decisions.
Halpern--Pearl weak and actual cause problems have definition-dependent hardness classifications.
The updated Halpern--Pearl definition changes the exact complexity of computing actual causes.
Binary acyclic Halpern--Pearl actual-cause checking can be encoded as satisfiability.
Binary Halpern--Pearl checking and inference can be formulated as ILP and MaxSAT optimization.
Adjustable beam search approximately identifies Halpern--Pearl-style causes in non-Boolean and stochastic systems.

tldr: Beckers defines actual causation by counterfactual dependence in an actualized structural simplification, but the definition has no exact algorithmic frontier. Under the backend-motivated computational restrictions of finite explicit local tables and a full graph on \(U\cup V\) whose undirected skeleton is a forest, the project derives a cost-preserving compiler and a complete value-path certificate. A linear-arithmetic dynamic program returns a witness and optimum certificate or a separating cut, while a selector-and-clause construction proves NP-completeness even when every variable is binary and deterministic and the endogenous graph is one directed chain. A parameterized shared-selector family pinpoints why the endogenous value-set state used in classical Halpern--Pearl causal-tree propagation cannot by itself audit Beckers deletion legality, without modifying the published Halpern--Pearl theorem.

project_justification.gap: Section 6, Proposition 20 on page 525, with proof on page 532, of Beckers2025Actual supplies a same-signature structural-simplification representative but no compiler, certificate system, minimum-cost result, or complexity classification. Existing causal-tree algorithms and SAT encodings concern Halpern--Pearl causation and do not enforce Beckers's full-graph reachability legality or actual-row freezing.
project_justification.niche: The novel computational scope restricts attention to finite explicitly encoded tables and, for the positive result, a forest skeleton on the full vertex set \(U\cup V\). These backend-motivated restrictions make row-level support auditing and unique-path composition possible without attributing them to Beckers or Eiter--Lukasiewicz.
project_justification.fill: The project proves an extensional compiler theorem, an exact additive optimum formula with independently checkable positive, optimality, and negative certificates, and a restricted NP-completeness theorem. The parameterized shared-selector obstruction shows precisely why two deletion histories with the same endogenous value state can differ in full-graph legality.

related_work: Beckers2025Actual, Section 5.1, Definitions 13, 15, and 16 on pages 523--524 and Section 6, Definitions 18 and 19 and Proposition 20 on page 525, supplies the structural-simplification and actual-causation semantics that the compiler must implement; the proof of Proposition 20 appears on page 532. It is semantic prior art and contains no algorithmic frontier. Beckers2025NCM supplies set-valued equations and topological counterfactual semantics, but the finite explicit encoding imposed here is a novel computational-scope restriction rather than a standard Beckers assumption. The earlier UAI version of EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable, Section 4.1 and Theorems 4.2--4.3, is the closest methodological comparator: its Halpern--Pearl causal-tree analysis recursively stores families of subsets of each endogenous path-variable domain. Its published theorem is left intact; the proposition for \(\mathcal O_{\kappa}\) shows only that a direct transfer of that unaugmented \(G[V]\)-only state type to Beckers deletion legality loses shared-exogenous reachability information. Requiring the full graph on \(U\cup V\) to be a polyforest is therefore a novel backend scope condition, not the causal-tree condition of EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable. EiterLukasiewicz2002Complexity and AleksandrowiczEtAl2014 show that complexity is definition-sensitive, but neither result concerns Beckers's deletion operation or full exogenous graph. IbrahimRehwaldPretschner2019SAT proves a Boolean SAT translation for Halpern--Pearl checking, while IbrahimPretschner2020Optimization attaches optimization objectives to binary Halpern--Pearl constraints. ReydDiaconescuDessalles2025Search motivates software-facing non-Boolean and stochastic search, but its adjustable beam search targets Halpern--Pearl-style causes and does not give exact negative or optimum certificates. These sources inform the semantics, propagation, reduction, and compiler architecture; no theorem-level extension of their estimands or encodings is claimed.
technical_internal_limitation: The full-unicycle question is intentionally unresolved. No claim is made for general full-graph treewidth, succinct mechanisms, continuous domains, negative deletion costs, unrestricted polynomial negative certificates, or unrestricted parsimonious counting. The selector reduction gives a bijection only after normalizing certificates; unrestricted successful graphs can encode one satisfying assignment in several ways and normalization need not preserve cost.
honest_scope: The local hitting lemma, forest completion, optimum recurrence, rational arithmetic bound, shared-selector obstruction, and selector implications are theorem obligations despite strong finite presolve evidence. The central unresolved verification task is the end-to-end arbitrary-domain compiler and independent verifier, including the order of actual-row freezing, preservation of the retained graph and charged deletions, and topological completion. Finiteness, explicit table encoding, and requiring the full graph on \(U\cup V\) to be a polyforest are novel computational-scope restrictions motivated by the backend rather than assumptions inherited from Beckers or Eiter--Lukasiewicz. As a sanity reduction, when all tables are deterministic and the full graph is a directed tree, the certificate becomes unique-path value propagation of the same structural form as the known causal-tree recurrence, while retaining Beckers rather than Halpern--Pearl local semantics.

The proof boundary is the absence of any finite certificate or complexity theorem.
seed_details.kernel: Exact minimum-cost value-path certificates on full causal polyforests, paired with NP-completeness on deterministic binary endogenous chains through shared exogenous selectors.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Halpern--Pearl contingency propagation by actualize-then-project bad-support hitting, and carry deleted-edge reachability in the full graph.
seed_details.destination_pair_search: Searches for Beckers structural simplification with algorithms, complexity, certificates, forests, and polyforests located no matching theorem; the nearest results were Beckers's semantics, Halpern--Pearl tree algorithms, and approximate package search.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is not a default SCM effect-identification or bounding problem: the query is already semantically defined, and the new object is an exact certificate-and-complexity frontier.

seed_details.rebuttal: That paper propagates Halpern--Pearl admissible-value sets through an endogenous causal-tree decomposition and its theorem is not disputed. The family \(\mathcal O_{\kappa}\) instead shows that two Beckers deletion histories can have identical endogenous layer states but different legality because of a retained path from a shared exogenous selector root.

novelty_justification: The closest published positive result is EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable; in its earlier UAI version, Section 4.1 and Theorems 4.2--4.3 decide Halpern--Pearl causes on bounded endogenous causal trees by recursively propagating families of subsets of path-variable domains. The proposed theorem changes the semantic operation at the first local step: it freezes the actual full parent row, unions outputs over deleted parent coordinates, and separately enforces full-graph reachability closure. The family \(\mathcal O_{\kappa}\) makes the separation exact: two candidate histories have the same \(G[V]\) layer and endogenous feasible-value state, but deletion of \(T_i\to C_i\) is legal only in the history that already removed \(T_i\to S_i\). This is a non-representability statement for a direct \(G[V]\)-only transfer of the unaugmented causal-tree state type to Beckers legality, not a criticism or alteration of the published Halpern--Pearl theorem. The closest semantic result is Section 6, Proposition 20 on page 525, with proof on page 532, of Beckers2025Actual, which guarantees a same-signature representative that simplifies both the original and actualized model but gives no encoded iff, optimum, certificate, or resource bound. Finiteness, explicit table encoding, and the full graph on \(U\cup V\) being a polyforest are novel backend-motivated computational restrictions rather than assumptions attributed to either comparator. The restricted hardness theorem shows that even a deterministic binary endogenous chain is hard once shared exogenous roots encode deletion legality. No located paper contains either half, and the joint positive-negative classification is stronger than a weighted version of a known tree recurrence or a generic SAT compilation.
